title: Jekyll and Hyde GCSE Revision: Themes, Key Quotations, Context & Essay Planning
description: Revise Jekyll and Hyde for GCSE English Literature with key themes, versatile quotations, Victorian context, narrative structure and practical essay planning.

children: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde rewards students who understand not only duality but also the way Stevenson controls information. The novella is a mystery before it becomes a confession, so narrative structure is part of its meaning.
Core themes
Duality and the divided self.
Reputation, secrecy and social respectability.
Science, transgression and the limits of knowledge.
Repression, desire and hidden behaviour.
Violence, degeneration and fears about civilisation.
Friendship, isolation and failed communication.
Versatile public-domain quotations

Short quotations worth knowing include 'man is not truly one, but truly two', 'ape-like fury', 'Satan's signature', 'profound duplicity of life', 'my devil had been long caged', and 'the moment I choose, I can be rid of Mr Hyde'.
Victorian context with a purpose
Rapid scientific development created excitement and anxiety about challenging religious and moral boundaries.
Ideas around evolution and degeneration can illuminate Hyde's repeated association with something primitive or less fully human.
Middle-class respectability helps explain the importance of reputation, secrecy and the male professional world of Utterson, Jekyll and Lanyon.
Gothic conventions allow hidden spaces, doubles, violence and the uncanny to externalise fears respectable society tries to suppress.
Use narrative structure as analysis

The reader spends much of the novella following Utterson's limited viewpoint. Full explanations arrive late through Lanyon's narrative and Jekyll's statement. That delayed revelation creates mystery and forces the reader to reinterpret earlier events.
Extract-to-whole-novella method
Build a thesis about Stevenson's presentation, not merely the named theme.
Analyse two or three precise details from the extract.
Connect the extract to earlier and later stages of the mystery.
Use structural ideas such as concealment, delayed revelation or shifting viewpoint where relevant.
Link Victorian context directly to interpretation.
Common mistakes
Writing a generic paragraph about Victorian repression regardless of the question.
Treating Jekyll and Hyde as completely separate and ignoring Jekyll's responsibility.
Describing Hyde as evil without analysing how Stevenson constructs that response.
Ignoring how Utterson's viewpoint shapes what the reader knows.
Using scientific context as a fact dump.
A high-value revision task

Choose one quotation about Jekyll and one about Hyde. Write three different thesis statements that could use both: one on duality, one on reputation and one on science. This trains flexible evidence rather than single-purpose memorisation.
